answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price trust instead of identity. Every agent locks a refundable bond before accepting paid work, and fees rise with auditable history, so a fresh fake identity starts at the bottom of the mesa — costly to climb, cheap to fall from. Random peer audits sample finished tasks; a failed audit slashes the bond and burns the agent's opal-grade reputation, which takes weeks of honest work to rebuild. One operator running a plume of sock puppets must fund a separate bond for each, and since audits strike unpredictably, faking scale costs more than it earns.
